result_summary: Dispatcher open AND close both proven against Demo through the full receipt -> Risk Boy -> dispatcher path; account FLAT

gate_chain_proof.note: A VETOED receipt was presented to the dispatcher FIRST. It threw 'Cannot dispatch unapproved receipt' and zero venue calls were made. I-02/I-03 hold on the Demo venue.

defect_found_and_fixed.root_cause: OrderDispatcher derived clientOid from receipt.receiptHash alone. An open and a close built from identical receipt data therefore produced the SAME clientOid, and the venue refused the second call as a duplicate. This made a full dispatcher lifecycle impossible on the venue.
defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_matters: It also invalidated an earlier claim: the Phase D pre-flight packet asserted that a receipt-derived clientOid gives safe retry idempotency. That was true for a RETRY of one intent but wrong for two DIFFERENT intents sharing receipt data. The claim is now corrected in the ledgers.
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: clientOid = sha256(receiptHash + ':' + intent)[0:32] — stable per intent, distinct across intents

net_position_accounting.explanation: Attempt 1 opened 0.001 via the dispatcher but its close was rejected (40786), leaving a residual short. Attempt 2 opened and closed its own 0.001, netting the account back to one open 0.001. A final dispatcher close flattened it.

orders_this_phase.note: attempt 1 open; its close was rejected 40786
attempt 2 close — proves dispatcher close path on venue

limitations: Bitget DEMO TRADING only. No real capital.
Proven on venue: dispatcher open -> fill, dispatcher close -> fill, veto gate blocks before any network call, account returns flat.
All four orders were 0.001 BTCUSDT (~83 USD notional). No sizing sweep, no partial fills, no limit orders, no multiple symbols.
NOT proven: cancel path (cancel-order endpoint still unimplemented in the dispatcher), SL/TP, leverage changes, funding accrual across an interval, liquidation.
NOT proven: live-venue execution of any kind.
NOT proven: continuous operation. Four bounded orders across two runs; no daemon, no loop, no scheduling.
